name: TX-03
label: Likely R

key_factors: R+11 district with incumbent Keith Self renominated and holding a clear cash advantage
Prediction markets price Self around 94%; no polls or expert ratings show a competitive race
Hunt's fundraising is modest and he has little cash on hand for the fall
A midterm environment favoring Democrats could narrow the margin
model.rationale: The district's double-digit Republican lean, Self's incumbency and financial edge, and markets pricing him near certain leave no evidence of a competitive race; Hunt's fundraising shows effort but little cash on hand to sustain a campaign. A friendlier midterm environment for Democrats may trim the margin without seriously threatening the seat.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing Hunt within single digits, or a sharply stronger Democratic national environment, would be the main signals of a genuine contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Texas's 3rd District, a suburban Dallas-area seat, leans strongly Republican, and incumbent Keith Self is running for reelection after being renominated. Challenger Evan Hunt has raised a modest sum but enters the fall with limited cash on hand, while Self holds the financial edge and draws outside support. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets give Self roughly a 94% chance of winning.

The structural picture points to a comfortable Republican hold. A national environment favoring Democrats could narrow the margin in a midterm year, but flipping a double-digit Republican seat would require a far larger wave than current evidence suggests. The forecast treats this as a likely Republican hold, with uncertainty driven mainly by the absence of local polling.
